# WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL is unstable at the dev head: vessel placement hand-off, a closed target during the placement wait, and a main-window claim tie on the last frame

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs` (#18047 / PR #18051, corner anchor from #18059) proves the popup-over-popup native titlebar drop under the Brain root. It runs in no CI workflow, so its health surfaces only when someone runs it by hand — as happened three times today.

Measured 2026-09-02, same machine, same tree, themes built:

| where | runs | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| dev head `99b5be2a23` (detached checkout, same tree) | 3 | 0 passed — run 1 `placing the target vessel did not hand it to the main window`; runs 2 + 3 `page.waitForTimeout: Target page, context or browser has been closed` at the `target.popup.waitForTimeout(800)` after placing the target vessel |
| PR #18119's branch (6ef4cf9780, on that head) | 5 across the afternoon | 2 passed, 3 failed — every failure `the last claim resolution names the target vessel`: `claimedStableId: "workstation-main"` where `workstation-vessel:metrics` was expected |
| Mnemosyne, earlier today, dev@f6811898ed and the #18112 branch | 3 + 3 | 1 passed each — the closed-target symptom |

`WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` (popup → main) is 1/1 on every run today, before and after each change.

## The Problem

Three distinct symptoms, all in the spec's setup or its first frames, none in the commit it exists to prove:

1. **Placement hand-off** — `placing the target vessel did not hand it to the main window`: after the target vessel is placed beside the main window, the workspace's `tearOutPanes[TARGET_ITEM].windowId` does not read the target's window id in time.
2. **Closed target during the placement wait** — the target popup is gone when the spec's `waitForTimeout(800)` on it resumes; a passing run logs `target popup closed` itself, so a close is part of the flow and the race is in WHEN it lands (Mnemosyne's reading).
3. **Main-window claim tie on the last frame** — the claim trace's last entry names `workstation-main`. The claim arbiter breaks a same-tick tie lexicographically, and `workstation-main` sorts before `workstation-vessel:…`; so on that frame BOTH windows intersected the source's corner anchor. The vessel is placed from `readScreen(page)` at `mainScreen.screenX + mainScreen.innerWidth` — outside the main window's LIVE frame — but the claim hit-tests `manager.Window` rects, which refresh only on a position change (#18068's note): after the spec's conditional shrink of the main window, a stale `outerRect` can still reach under the vessel.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs#getNativeWindowDropCandidate` → `resolveClaimedTarget` (arbiter, same-tick tie → lexicographic) and `getWindowAtExcept` (`Window.items.find(item.outerRect.intersects(point))`).
- `src/manager/Window.mjs` — rects refresh on connect / position change; a resize without a move leaves `outerRect` stale.
- The spec: `readScreen`-based placement, conditional shrink (`stage.availLeft + 760 + 20 + 200 > …`), `test.skip` gate on chrome height, `awaitOriginParity` after each CDP move, the 800 ms target-placement wait.

## The Fix

Attribution first, then the smallest change that makes the spec deterministic:

1. Instrument one failing run of each symptom with the spec's own diagnostic (the coordinator's `claimTrace` with candidates, `manager.Window.toJSON()` rects for main and both vessels, the target popup's `closed` state timeline) and pin which window's rect is stale or which close fires.
2. If (3) is the stale main `outerRect` after the shrink: publish geometry after the spec's resize (the `WindowPosition` addon's `publishGeometry`, or a real move-by-zero through CDP so the manager refreshes), and assert the manager's main rect no longer reaches under the vessel before the first nudge.
3. If (2) is a genuine close of the target vessel (a retirement racing the placement), read the retire receipt on the failing run and file the engine defect it names separately; the spec then waits on a state, not on 800 ms.
4. Land the spec fixes with a 5× local run record in the PR body; the spec stays out of CI until it is deterministic.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-02T18:06:09Z

## AC-1, symptom (3): attributed — and the stated cause is not the one

Taking this lane (@tobiu asked the Opus seats to drive more while the Fable flatrate is at 98%). Starting with source-level attribution before spending headed runs, and symptom (3) resolves without any: **the mechanism the ticket suspects is missing is present and armed. The defect is that it is unbarriered.**

### What the ticket proposed

> a stale `outerRect` can still reach under the vessel … If (3) is the stale main `outerRect` after the shrink: publish geometry after the spec's resize (the `WindowPosition` addon's `publishGeometry`, or a real move-by-zero through CDP so the manager refreshes)

That prescription assumes publication does not happen on a resize. It does.

### What the source says

- **`WindowPosition#onResize` already publishes.** `src/main/addon/WindowPosition.mjs:285` ends with `me.publishGeometry()`, under a comment naming this exact case: *"A fixed-origin resize is still a geometry change. The conversion metric consumes live extents every frame, so movement-only publication would make its post-resize decision stale."*
- **The observer is armed on every dock window.** `observeResize_` defaults to `false` (`:44`), but `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:990` calls `setConfigs({observeMovement: true, observeResize: true, windowId})` per window, and its JSDoc (`:975-976`) explains why both default off and are turned on there. So a resize on a Workstation window does reach `onResize`.
- **A second path covers programmatic mutation.** `src/Main.mjs#publishWindowGeometry(win)` publishes the *target realm's* snapshot after a mutation, explicitly to close "the mutation-to-observation edge".

So `checkMovement`'s position-only comparison (`:156`) is not the gap — it is only the *poll's* trigger. Resize has its own, correct trigger.

### The actual cause

`publishGeometry()` is **fire-and-forget across a thread boundary**:

```js
publishGeometry() {
    let {Manager} = Neo.worker,
        winData   = Neo.Main.getWindowData();

    Manager.sendMessage('app', {action: 'windowPositionChange', data: {…winData, windowId}})
}
```

No return value, no `await`, and no call site awaits it — I grepped every one. The chain is:

`resize` (main thread) → `onResize` → `publishGeometry` → `sendMessage` → **cross-thread hop** → `App.onWindowPositionChange` → `manager.Window` rect update (app worker)

and the claim arbiter runs **in the app worker**, against those rects: `DragCoordinator#getWindowAtExcept` → `Window.items.find(item.outerRect.intersects(point))`.

**So between the resize landing on the main thread and the new rect landing in `manager.Window`, there is a window of frames in which the arbiter hit-tests the pre-resize `outerRect`.** That is exactly the reported symptom: main's stale, larger frame still reaches under the placed vessel, both windows intersect the corner anchor on the same tick, and the lexicographic tie-break returns `workstation-main` — which sorts before `workstation-vessel:…`.

The mechanism is correct. It has no happens-before edge with the thing that consumes it.

### What this changes about the fix

**Adding another `publishGeometry()` call after the spec's shrink would not help** — publication is already happening; a second fire-and-forget message creates no barrier. The fix has to be a *wait on the observation*, not another emission:

- The spec should poll `manager.Window`'s main row until its `outerRect` reflects the shrunk size, and only then perform the first nudge — asserting a state, exactly as the ticket's own item 3 prescribes for symptom (2). That converts an implicit race into an explicit precondition.
- AC-2's "asserts the state instead of waiting on time" is therefore the right shape for symptom (3) as well, not only for (2).

### The engine question this raises, deliberately not bundled

Whether the *claim path itself* should tolerate an unobserved resize is a larger question than this spec: today any consumer of `manager.Window` rects can read them mid-flight after a resize, and only this spec happens to notice. That is worth its own ticket rather than a change smuggled into a test-stability fix — I have not filed it yet, because I would rather attribute symptoms (1) and (2) first and see whether they share this cause. If they do, one engine ticket covers all three.

Symptoms (1) and (2) next; the headed determinism runs come after the 5-hour bucket resets.

🖖 Grace


### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-02T18:11:40Z

## AC-1, symptoms (1) and (2): attributed — all three share one shape, and it is mostly spec-side

Continuing the source-level attribution. The three symptoms looked distinct in the ticket; they are one shape wearing three costumes: **the spec waits on TIME for states that arrive ASYNCHRONOUSLY across a boundary.** Where they differ is which side owes the fix.

### Symptom (1) — placement hand-off

`placing the target vessel did not hand it to the main window` is `tearOutPanes[TARGET_ITEM].windowId` not reading the target's id. That write happens in exactly one place:

```js
// src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:944
reparentTearOutPane(itemId, target = {}) {
    let {windowId} = target,
        app        = Neo.apps[windowId],
        pane       = me.resolveTearOutPane(itemId);

    if (!app || !pane || pane.isDestroyed) return false;      // ← the early return
    …
    me.tearOutPanes[itemId] && Object.assign(me.tearOutPanes[itemId], target);   // :966
    return true
}
```

The assignment is gated on `Neo.apps[windowId]` already existing. A freshly placed vessel window boots its own app, and that registration lands in the shared worker **after** the window exists — so a reparent attempted in the interval returns `false` silently and the hand-off never happens. Not an engine defect: you cannot reparent a pane into an app that has not registered. The defect is that the spec's `waitForTimeout(800)` is a **guess at how long registration takes**, not a wait for registration.

### Symptom (2) — closed target during the placement wait

Same shape, and Mnemosyne's own reading in the ticket already contains the answer: *"a passing run logs `target popup closed` itself, so a close is part of the flow and the race is in WHEN it lands."* A fixed 800 ms either lands before or after a close that is legitimately part of the flow. The spec is asserting a coin-flip.

### Symptom (3) — main-window claim tie

Attributed in my previous comment: the resize-publication mechanism is present and armed, but `publishGeometry()` is fire-and-forget across a thread boundary while the claim arbiter reads `manager.Window` rects **in the app worker**. Unbarriered, so the arbiter can hit-test a pre-resize rect.

### What this means for the fix

**Two of the three are spec-side, and AC-2's own wording already prescribes the remedy** — *"asserts the state instead of waiting on time"* — it just needs applying to all three rather than only to (2):

| symptom | wait on TIME (today) | wait on STATE (fix) |
|---|---|---|
| (1) placement hand-off | `waitForTimeout(800)` | poll until `Neo.apps[targetWindowId]` is live **and** `tearOutPanes[TARGET_ITEM].windowId` equals it |
| (2) closed target | `target.popup.waitForTimeout(800)` | poll the state the close is part of, and tolerate a closed page rather than touching it afterwards |
| (3) claim tie | implicit — none | poll `manager.Window`'s main row until its `outerRect` reflects the shrink, before the first nudge |

**One engine question survives, and it is (3) alone.** (1) and (2) are the spec mis-waiting on correct engine behaviour. (3) is different in kind: any consumer of `manager.Window` rects can read them mid-flight after a resize, and this spec merely happens to notice. I will file that separately with the receipt once the spec fixes are in, rather than smuggling an engine change into a test-stability PR — and now that (1) and (2) are attributed, I can say it does **not** share their cause, so one ticket for (3) is the right shape rather than one covering all three.

### Sequencing, given the demo

The spec runs in no CI workflow, so none of this is blocking tomorrow morning — and I would rather not touch a cross-window path the night before a rehearsal for a test-only gain. Plan: land the three state-waits and the 5× determinism record after the demo, and file the (3) engine ticket alongside. If anyone needs `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` green before then, say so and I will reprioritise — but its instability is in the spec's setup, not in the commit it exists to prove, and `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` (popup → main) has been 1/1 on every run today.

Attribution is AC-1 complete for all three symptoms.

🖖 Grace
